config.providers.description: LLM services that speak the OpenAI chat API. Each entry has a unique `name`, a `baseUrl`, the API root such as `http://localhost:11434/v1`, and an optional `caFile` for a corporate or self-signed certificate. API keys are stored in the editor's secret storage, never here. Read from user settings only: a workspace cannot override this list, so a repository cannot redirect a stored key.
config.providers.name.description: Unique name shown in the chat panel.
config.providers.baseUrl.description: API root, for example `http://localhost:11434/v1`. broke-code appends `/models` and `/chat/completions`.
config.providers.caFile.description: Optional PEM file of extra certificate authorities to trust for this provider only, such as a corporate or self-signed CA. Absolute path, or starting with `~/`. It adds to the system certificates, never replaces them. Certificate verification cannot be turned off.
config.contextSizes.description: Context size of each model, in tokens, by model name as the provider lists it, for example `{ "gemma-4": 262144, "qwen3:8b": 40960 }`. A model absent from this table, or with a size that is not a positive whole number, uses 32,768. An agent turn stops before a request whose estimated size (characters divided by the characters per token learned from the replies, 4 at first) leaves less than one eighth of the context for the reply, even with older tool results left out, unless `brokeCode.autoCompact` summarizes the conversation first. Read from user settings only.
config.maxToolSteps.description: Tool steps an agent turn may take before it stops: tool calls, each call a Code Mode script makes included, and malformed calls alike. At least 1. A turn in flight keeps the limit it started with. Read from user settings only.
config.autoCompact.description: When an agent turn's next request would not fit the model's context, even with older tool results left out, ask the model for a summary of the conversation, as `/compact` does, and go on with the turn instead of stopping it. The request then sends the summary and the turn's message in place of everything before them. At most one summary per request. Off by default, since it adds a request you did not ask for. A turn reads it when it starts. Read from user settings only.
config.mode.description: How the agent's file changes (`write_file`, `edit_file`) and commands (`run_command`) are approved. **Ask** (default): each change waits for Accept and each command for Run. **Auto-edit**: changes are written without asking; commands still wait for Run. **Full access**: changes are written and commands run without asking. Each command then runs in a macOS sandbox that refuses any write outside the workspace folders, the temporary folders, `~/Library/Caches`, `~/.cache`, and the package caches `~/.bun/install/cache`, `~/.npm`, `~/.cargo/registry`, `~/.cargo/git`, `~/go/pkg/mod`, `~/.gradle/caches`, and `~/.m2/repository` (caches only, never a folder of installed programs such as `~/.cargo/bin`); reads and the network stay open. A command matching one of `#brokeCode.deniedCommands#` is refused without running. The chat marks each step approved this way as auto-approved. A file with unsaved changes in an editor is never written. Read from user settings only: a workspace cannot weaken approval. The mode selector in the chat's message box shows this setting and writes it. As a user setting, it applies to every window. Its fourth mode, Plan, kept per workspace, gives the agent the read tools only and leaves this setting as it is.
config.mode.ask: Each change waits for Accept and each command for Run.
config.mode.autoEdit: Changes are written without asking. Commands still wait for Run.
config.mode.fullAccess: Changes are written and commands run without asking, commands in a sandbox that keeps their writes inside the workspace.
config.deniedCommands.description: Commands **Full access** refuses without running them, in addition to the built-in ones: `sudo`, `su`, `doas`, `open`, `osascript`, `launchctl`, `defaults`, `security`, `crontab`, `diskutil`, `shutdown`, `reboot`, `halt`, `git push --force`, `git push -f`, `git reset --hard`, `git clean`. Each entry is a program, words its command must hold in order, then flags it must hold anywhere: `git push --force` also refuses `git push origin main --force`. Each simple command of a line is checked (`a && b`, pipes, `$(...)`), the program by its file name. This list only catches a known risky command early: a command can be written to slip past it, so the sandbox is the guard. It never removes a built-in entry, and the other modes ignore it. Read at each command, from user settings only: a workspace cannot change it.
config.commandTimeoutSeconds.description: Seconds a command the agent runs (`run_command`) may take before its process group is stopped: SIGTERM, then SIGKILL two seconds later. A process that left the group (setsid, a daemon) is not stopped. The model gets the output so far. At least 1. Read at each command, from user settings only: a workspace cannot change it.
config.notifications.description: Show a notification when an agent turn or `/compact` ends, fails, or stops on a limit, or when a file change or a command waits for your decision, while the chat is not in view: the chat view is hidden, or the window does not have the focus. Each notification has a Show chat button. A turn you stop shows none. On by default. Read at each event, from user settings only: only the user value `false` turns the notifications off.
config.codeMode.description: Experimental. Lets the agent write one JavaScript script that calls several of its tools in a single reply, such as the same change in several files, and read back only what the script prints. Scripts run in a macOS sandbox that reads none of your files, writes nothing, and reaches no network, so they act only through the tools, and each tool call a script makes asks for your approval and counts as one tool step, as a direct call does, in every mode. It may change or be removed in a later version. Read from user settings only: a workspace cannot turn it on.
